pairs.why: A's gold-rimmed visor, riveted collar ring and rimmed ear disc look like a built object, like the submarine's porthole rims; B is a plainer, softer shell that reads more like a toy.
B has the gold visor rim, riveted collar and framed side disc, matching the trimmed-part construction of the real cards, while A is a simpler, blobbier shell.
A's thick gold visor rim and bezelled side disc give the clear part breakdown the real submarine and ring box show; B's rimless visor looks unfinished.
B frames the visor with a gold rim like the real porthole bezels, while A has a rimless visor; the two are otherwise close in finish.
B's rock has slightly cleaner, smoother crater forms and a warm rim light that ties it to the background, while A's surface is grainier and frostier, which the lessons mark as too texture-y.
A has the smoother rock with a warm rim light; B's rock is grittier and more speckled, against the smooth soft finish of the real scarf, fan and pillow.
A has a few large, soft craters on a smoother ball, while B adds many small, crisp crater details and sharper surface grain, the over-texture the lessons penalise.
A's rock is rounder, softer and lighter in finish, close to the smooth, slightly matte real cards, while B's is grainier, with busier crater texture.
